research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) — Reorder Point / Fixed Order Quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (98.5% non-zero) with moderate variability and no trend, making a classic (r,Q) model appropriate. The high ordering cost relative to unit holding cost favours large batch sizes, which the EOQ captures well. A base-stock or (s,S) policy would add complexity without benefit given the stable, non-intermittent demand pattern.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is a binding constraint: the unconstrained EOQ (2,931 units) exceeds available space after safety stock (1,472 units remaining). This forces more frequent ordering than optimal, slightly increasing annual ordering costs versus the pure EOQ outcome. Any upward revision of safety stock must be matched by a corresponding reduction in order quantity to remain within 1,625.7 units.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (132) + safety stock (153) = 285 units, well within storage capacity of 1,625.7 units. No MOQ-capacity infeasibility. Monitor: if safety stock requirements grow (e.g., due to further lead time deterioration), the capacity constraint will tighten further.
